slices.title: Complete authentication-material cleanup and add regression coverage
slices.notes: Token removal already done in adoption commit. Complete remaining cleanup: confirm no fallback credentials remain, add token/credential redaction in logs, add .device and secret files to .gitignore, add make test-security target with tests proving credentials are never embedded/logged, add security documentation. Report that token rotation and git-history cleanup remain manual security operations.

slices.title: Make Hermes supervisor handoffs deterministic
slices.notes: Run Hermes in scripted one-shot mode with `hermes chat -q -Q` and HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1. Capture final response, validate JSON syntax and slice_id, write handoff atomically via temp file + mv. Adapter owns JSON file writing, not Hermes.

slices.title: Add an offline-safe authentication diagnostic command
slices.notes: Add diagnostic behavior with mocked responses. Do not perform account mutations.

slices.title: Harden adapter portability and handoff robustness
slices.notes: Replace hardcoded Python paths in Makefile with portable discovery. Add adapter-level schema validation against handoff.schema.json. Make handoff write truly atomic (temp + rename). Remove stale 'hermes -z' reference from queue notes. Add adapter test with fake Hermes executable.

slices.title: Inventory current gameplay capabilities against the roadmap (AUTO-001)
slices.notes: R0/AUTO-001. Add docs/baseline/capability-inventory.json mapping every public sdk.client.Client method and run.py flag to a roadmap pillar (A-F), a mutating/read-only flag, and an evidence level (mocked-test, live-claimed, untested) citing the test file or README claim that supports it. Add docs/baseline/capability-inventory.md summarising gaps per release R1-R3. Add a test that fails when a public Client method is missing from the inventory, so the map cannot drift. Correct the outdated offline-only roadmap sentence in README.template, then regenerate README.md. No network traffic; do not claim live behaviour that is not already documented.

slices.title: Add a typed, account-scoped game state snapshot (AUTO-002)
slices.notes: R1/AUTO-002. Add sdk/state/ with a frozen AccountSnapshot (account alias, observed_at, source, game_version, per-section completeness, hull level, trophies, resources, crew, rooms, research, inventory) and a pure builder from already-parsed client response dicts. Missing sections are marked partial, never invented. Reject secret-shaped keys using sdk.redaction. Refuse to merge or diff snapshots from different account aliases. Tests use synthetic fixtures only.

slices.title: Add a typed gameplay action catalog with postcondition reconciliation (AUTO-003)
slices.notes: R1/AUTO-003. Add sdk/actions/ with ActionSpec records (action id, Client method, mutating flag, idempotency class, preconditions, expected snapshot delta) for representative actions: collect all resources, collect daily reward, add training, upgrade room, add research. Add reconcile(spec, before, after) returning VERIFIED, NOT_OBSERVED, CONTRADICTED or UNKNOWN; an HTTP success alone is never VERIFIED. Pure functions; synthetic before/after snapshot tests for every outcome.

slices.title: Add an append-only, redacted gameplay event journal (R1 observability)
slices.notes: R1 evidence layer. Add sdk/journal.py: JSONL events with account alias, action id, attempt id, timestamps, expected effect, observed outcome, reconciliation status, error class and cost fields. Redact through sdk.redaction before writing; refuse secret-shaped values. Provide a reader and a per-account summary (attempted, verified, uncertain, failed). Tests write to temporary directories only.

slices.title: Execute catalog actions with before/after snapshots, reconciliation and journaling (R1 exit)
slices.notes: R1 exit. Add sdk/execution/ with a runner that takes an injected client and snapshot provider, checks preconditions, captures before and after snapshots, invokes one catalog action, reconciles it and journals the result. Timeouts, exceptions and ambiguous responses are journaled explicitly as uncertain; no automatic retry of non-idempotent actions; a dry-run mode performs no mutating call. Refuse to run when the snapshot alias differs from the requested account. Tests use a fake client; no real network traffic. Do not wire it into run.py yet.

slices.title: Build account snapshots from Client reads (R2 input)
slices.notes: R2 prerequisite. Add sdk/state/client_provider.py: a snapshot provider that calls only read-only Client methods (getShipByUserId, listAllCharactersOfUser, listItemsOfAShip and the resource totals the client already tracks) and feeds build_snapshot for a given alias. A read that fails or returns no data leaves its section missing; it never raises past the provider unless the alias is invalid. It must never call a mutating method, enforced by a test whose fake client fails on any method the capability inventory marks mutating. Fake-client tests only; no network traffic.

slices.title: Observe crew training state so add_training can be verified
slices.notes: Extend CrewMember with training_design_id and training_end (from @TrainingDesignId and @TrainingEndDate when present; unknown otherwise) and include training changes in SnapshotDelta. Change the add_training postcondition: VERIFIED when the crew member gains the requested training, NOT_OBSERVED when training is observed and unchanged, UNKNOWN when training fields were not observed. Update docs/baseline/action-catalog.md. Synthetic tests for every outcome.

slices.title: Add a single-room upgrade call without changing upgradeRooms behaviour
slices.notes: Extract the existing per-room UpgradeRoom2 request inside Client.upgradeRooms into a public Client.upgradeRoom(roomId, upgradeRoomDesignId) method, and make upgradeRooms delegate to it so its room selection and resource checks are unchanged (preserve existing gameplay strategy; add a regression test pinning upgradeRooms' calls). Point the upgrade_room catalog spec and CALL_ARGUMENTS at the targeted method with an upgrade_room_design_id parameter. Add the method to docs/baseline/capability-inventory.json. Mocked requests only.

slices.title: Rank progression actions from a snapshot with a rule-based baseline policy (AUTO-005)
slices.notes: AUTO-005. Add sdk/policy/ with a pure, versioned policy interface: plan(snapshot, design_data, config) returns ordered ActionRequests (catalog action id, params, reason, expected cost) plus the candidates it rejected and why. Ship one policy, baseline-v1, that reproduces run.py's current daily order and resource checks as closely as the catalog allows, so automated runs can be compared against today's behaviour. Respect configurable mineral/gas reserves, skip actions whose preconditions fail, and never emit an action for an unobserved section. Design data (room upgrade costs, research costs) is passed in, not fetched. Synthetic tests only.

slices.title: Execute a policy plan through the runner with budgets, cooldowns and an operator stop (AUTO-004)
slices.notes: AUTO-004. Add sdk/scheduler/: run a policy plan for one account through ActionRunner, re-snapshotting between actions. Enforce once-per-period actions from journal history, a per-run action budget, a stop on the first CONTRADICTED or uncertain non-idempotent result, and an operator stop file checked before every action. Dry-run is the default; live execution needs an explicit execute=True argument. Fake client and temporary journal in tests; no network traffic. Do not wire into run.py.

slices.title: Add an offline-safe progression dry-run command to run.py
slices.notes: Add a run.py --progression-dry-run flag that authenticates as today, builds a snapshot through the client provider, plans with baseline-v1, and journals dry-run events to a local path (default under logs/, which must stay gitignored) without any mutating call. Print the plan and the rejected candidates. Mocked client in tests, including a test that fails if any mutating Client method is called. Document the flag in README.template, then README.md. No live execute flag in this slice.

slices.title: Report progression and reliability metrics from the journal (R2 exit metrics)
slices.notes: R2 exit evidence. Add sdk/reports/progression.py: from journal events, compute per-account, per-day verified actions, verified action success rate, uncertain and failed counts, resources gained and spent per elapsed hour (from cost deltas), and a failure ledger. Every metric reports its sample size and time window; with no events it reports empty, not zero rates. Output JSON and a Markdown table. Synthetic journals in temporary directories.

slices.title: Run baseline-v1 against an owned test account and compare with the manual routine
slices.entry_condition: Owner authorization required: confirm live automation runs on a named owned test account (credentials through the existing secret flow, never committed), define the manual baseline routine and the comparison window, then set this slice to queued. Live execution against a real account is not authorized yet.
slices.notes: R2 exit trial. Add an explicit live execute path for the scheduler, run it on the authorized test account for the agreed window, and record the progression metrics report against the manual baseline in docs/experiments/. Unit tests stay mocked; only the trial itself touches the live game.

slices.title: Treat present-but-empty snapshot containers as observed and empty
slices.notes: Defect found in r2-progression-dry-run-command: ClientSnapshotProvider marks rooms, research, crew or inventory as missing when the response contains the container element (Rooms, Researches, Characters, Items) with no records, so a new ship with no research never gets research planned. A present container with no records must yield an observed, empty section; an absent container or a failed read stays missing. Add regression tests, including one proving baseline-v1 plans research for a ship whose Researches element is empty. Update docs/baseline/account-snapshot.md.

slices.title: Versioned PvP strategy registry and experiment windows (AUTO-006)
slices.notes: R3 start. Add sdk/pvp/strategies.py: a PvP strategy is data (strategy_id, version, description, native AI rule set, room/crew role assignments by reference, power and targeting preferences) with a deterministic content hash as its config version. Add an experiment window model that assigns at most one strategy to an account alias per non-overlapping UTC window, and a lookup that returns the strategy active for an alias at a time (or None). Ship two candidate strategies as data. Pure and offline; reuse sdk.pvp models and compute_ship_config_version where they fit. Synthetic tests only.

slices.title: Catalog a PvP battle action whose outcome is observed, not assumed (AUTO-007)
slices.notes: Add a run_pvp_battle ActionSpec mapped to the existing Client.runBattleEndToEnd flow, non-idempotent, with preconditions (full ship HP when observed) and a postcondition that needs an observed outcome: a trophy change or a battle record from a fresh read. If no verified read-only method returns current trophies or battle history, the postcondition stays not-observed and the outcome is unknown; an HTTP success alone never yields verified. Record evidence tiers (request accepted, battle created, finalised, outcome observed) in the journal event. Do not change runBattleEndToEnd or the existing run.py battle behaviour. Mocked client only. Add an optional evidence mapping to GameplayEvent (schema-compatible: old journal lines without it still read) so the evidence tiers are stored as data, not parsed from reason text.

slices.title: Build PvP battle results from journaled battle events
slices.notes: Convert run_pvp_battle journal events into sdk.pvp BattleResult records: account alias as pseudonym, strategy id and version from the experiment window active at the event time, trophy delta only when observed, outcome unknown unless the event's evidence tier reached outcome observed. Label opponent cohorts (hull bracket, trophy bracket) when known and 'unknown' otherwise. Synthetic journals in temporary directories. The journal does not yet carry the observed trophy change: pass the snapshot delta to the action's evidence builder so run_pvp_battle evidence records trophies_delta (None when unobserved).

slices.title: Offense/defense scorecards and strategy comparison by opponent cohort (R3 exit metrics)
slices.notes: Add sdk/reports/pvp.py: per alias, strategy version and opponent cohort, report attacks and defenses with known results, wins, losses, win rates with 95% Wilson intervals, net trophies, mean duration and resource cost where observed, and unknown-outcome counts. Compare two strategies: recommend one only when both meet a minimum sample size and their intervals do not overlap; otherwise report insufficient evidence. No sample means no number. JSON and Markdown output.

slices.title: Run two PvP strategies on an owned test account and record the comparison
slices.entry_condition: Owner authorization required: confirm live PvP runs on a named owned test account (credentials through the existing secret flow, never committed), choose the two strategies and the experimental windows, then set this slice to queued. Live execution against a real account is not authorized yet.
slices.notes: R3 exit trial. Run each strategy for its window, then record the scorecard and recommendation in docs/experiments/. Unit tests stay mocked; only the trial itself touches the live game.

slices.title: Typed marketplace listings from ListActiveMarketplaceMessages (AUTO-008)
slices.notes: R4 start. Keep Client.listActiveMarketplaceMessages' request and logging unchanged, but also store the parsed messages on the client (for example self.marketplaceMessages) so they can be read without re-requesting. Add sdk/economy/market.py: a frozen MarketListing parsed from a message with whitelisted fields only (item design id, quantity, currency and price from @ActivityArgument, message/sale ids only when present), refusing secret-shaped values, and leaving unknown fields None rather than guessing. Mocked responses only; update the capability inventory entry's tests if the drift test requires it.

slices.title: Per-account currency and item ledger from snapshots and the journal
slices.notes: Add sdk/economy/ledger.py: from an ordered series of AccountSnapshots and journal events for one account, record minerals, gas, starbux and per-item quantity changes, attributing each change to the journaled action whose before/after window contains it and marking the rest unattributed. Unobserved values stay unknown, never zero. Refuse snapshots from another account. Pure and offline.

slices.title: Reconcile a market trade's lifecycle from observations, never from listing creation alone
slices.notes: Add sdk/economy/trades.py: a pure state machine for one trade (requested, listed, sold or purchased, expired, unknown) driven by observations: listing seen with an identity, the item leaving or entering inventory, the currency change, price and fees. A trade is complete only when the item and currency movements are both observed and consistent; a created listing alone is 'listed' at most. Record realized proceeds and fees when observed. Synthetic observations only.

slices.title: Market return and resource-allocation report (R4 exit metrics)
slices.notes: Add a report over reconciled trades and the ledger: per account and strategy/policy version, market return (realized proceeds minus purchase cost and fees, completed trades only), unreconciled trade count, resources gained and spent per elapsed hour, and spend by action. Every figure carries its sample size; no sample means no number. JSON and Markdown output.

slices.title: Implement and reconcile a live market trade on an owned test account
slices.entry_condition: Owner input required: provide current captures for SellItem3 and Purchase4 (sanitized, no tokens) so the client calls can be implemented against the installed game version, authorize live trades on a named owned test account, and define the economic experiment. Live execution against a real account is not authorized yet.
slices.notes: R4 exit trial. Implement SellItem3/Purchase4 from the provided captures, run the agreed trades, and record the reconciled outcomes and market return in docs/experiments/. Unit tests stay mocked.

slices.title: Account registry with objectives, budgets and strategy assignment (AUTO-009)
slices.notes: R5 start. Add sdk/fleet/accounts.py: an AccountProfile per alias (objective label, progression policy id, optional PvP strategy key, per-period resource spend budgets, max actions, enabled flag, and the NAME of the secret that holds its credentials, never a secret value). Load a registry from JSON with fail-closed validation: aliases follow the snapshot alias rule, aliases are unique, e-mail addresses and secret-shaped values are refused anywhere in the file. Pure and offline; synthetic files in temporary directories.

slices.title: Sequential fleet orchestration with per-account isolation and budgets
slices.notes: Add sdk/fleet/orchestrator.py: run the daily scheduler for each enabled account in turn, using injected per-account factories for the client, snapshot provider and journal, so no account ever receives another account's client, snapshots or journal. Enforce each account's spend budget by planning within it, stop one account on a safety stop without stopping the others, honour a fleet-wide stop file, and default to dry-run. Record per-account outcomes, elapsed time and the mode (sequential). Fakes only.

slices.title: Audit journals and snapshots for cross-account mix-ups
slices.notes: Add sdk/fleet/audit.py: given the registry and each account's journal, report incidents: events whose alias is not the journal's owner, aliases not in the registry, attempt ids reused across accounts, overlapping mutating attempts on one account, and spend above the account's budget for a period. Each incident names the account, event and rule. An empty report states how many events and accounts were checked.

slices.title: Fleet throughput, failure and isolation report (R5 exit metrics)
slices.notes: Add a fleet report: per account and fleet-wide, verified actions, attempted actions, failure and uncertain rates, actions per elapsed hour, isolation incidents from the audit, and the orchestration mode, so sequential and future concurrent runs compare on the same fields. Operator time saved is reported only when the operator supplies manual baseline minutes per account; otherwise it is None. JSON and Markdown output.

slices.title: Run the fleet orchestrator on two owned test accounts
slices.entry_condition: Owner authorization required: name at least two owned test accounts with credentials provisioned through the existing secret flow (never committed), supply each account's manual routine minutes, and authorize live fleet runs. Live execution against real accounts is not authorized yet.
slices.notes: R5 exit trial. Wire the orchestrator into run.py behind an explicit flag, run it on the authorized accounts, and record the fleet report and isolation audit in docs/experiments/. Unit tests stay mocked.

slices.title: Policy evaluation loop with recorded, versioned decisions (AUTO-011)
slices.notes: R6 start. Add sdk/experiments/: an Experiment record (id, hypothesis, baseline and candidate variants, primary metric, minimum sample per variant, window) and a decide function that turns measured samples into adopt, reject, keep-running or insufficient-evidence using 95% intervals, never adopting without the minimum sample. Decisions are appended to a JSONL decision log with the experiment, evidence and timestamp; nothing is rolled out automatically. Pure and offline.

slices.title: Deterministic offline gameplay scenarios end to end (AUTO-014)
slices.notes: Add sdk/simulation/: a deterministic fake game (resources, rooms, research, trophies) exposing the Client method names the catalog uses, seeded scenarios loaded from JSON, and a runner that drives registry -> fleet orchestrator -> journals -> progression, fleet and audit reports for a scenario, with no network. The same scenario and seed must give byte-identical reports. Ship two scenarios (single account, two accounts) and regression tests over them.

slices.title: Offline report command over journals
slices.notes: Add a run.py report mode that needs no login: given journal paths (and optionally a registry), print the progression, PvP, economy-from-journal or fleet report as Markdown or JSON and exit. It must not construct a game client or touch the network. Update README.template first, then README.md, and the capability inventory's run.py flags.

slices.title: Release instructions, known limitations and roadmap status (R6 docs)
slices.notes: Write release instructions (versioning, the CI gates, how a release is cut), a consolidated known-limitations page drawn from the baseline docs (unverified reads, unimplemented market endpoints, untrusted battle outcomes, blocked live trials), and update docs/PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md with what has actually merged per release and what remains blocked. Documentation only; no code changes.

slices.title: Automation effectiveness study report from live trials
slices.entry_condition: Requires the live trials (r2, r3, r4, r5) to have run with owner authorization and recorded results. Nothing live has been authorized yet.
slices.notes: R6 exit. Write the study report quantifying when automation helped, failed or cost more than manual play, from the recorded live trial evidence, with sample sizes and limitations.

slices.title: Enforce fleet budgets against the planning snapshot and reject unknown costs
slices.notes: Review defects: (1) the orchestrator computed reserves from its own snapshot while the scheduler planned from a later one, so balance growth became extra budget; (4) the policy treated a missing or unparseable room price, or a missing research starbux cost, as free. Add explicit spend caps to PolicyConfig that the policy applies against the snapshot it plans from, have the orchestrator pass remaining budget as caps, and reject candidates whose cost is unknown. Regression tests must fail on the old code.

slices.title: Never verify a battle outcome without a battle step; tolerate non-UTC journal times
slices.notes: Review defects: (3) a run_pvp_battle call that raised before any battle step was journaled verified with tier outcome-observed when an unrelated trophy change occurred, and reported as a win; (7) battles_from_events crashed on journal times not in UTC. Require a battle step for outcome-observed, downgrade such a verified outcome to unknown, require no error for win/loss, and normalise times to UTC before the schedule lookup. Regression tests must fail on the old code.

slices.title: Tighten trade completion and ledger attribution
slices.notes: Review defects: (5) buys completed on any item arrival plus any spend >= price with no upper bound, and sells completed from the item leaving at listing time plus any unrelated currency gain; (6) the ledger attributed a change to one action while another action overlapped the end of the interval; (10) sell listings matched any own listing at the same price. Bound buy cost and sell proceeds, require the listing to be gone and newly seen after the request, treat end-overlapping actions as candidates (ambiguous), and prefer item-design matches. Regression tests must fail on the old code.

slices.title: Robust experiment intervals and simulation correctness
slices.notes: Review defects: (8) MeanSample used a z interval from n >= 2 and zero variance gave zero-width intervals, so two measurements could adopt a variant; simulation charged nothing for gas-priced room upgrades and appended to existing journals when a workdir was reused, breaking byte-identical reports. Use a t-based interval, refuse decisions on zero-variance samples, charge gas prices, and start each scenario from empty journals. Regression tests must fail on the old code.

slices.title: Charge expected cost of uncertain attempts against budgets
slices.notes: Review defect (2): an attempt whose after-snapshot failed was journaled unknown with no cost, so neither spent_in_period nor the audit charged it and the next run started with the full budget. Pass the planned expected cost from the scheduler to the runner, record it as <kind>_uncertain cost for attempts whose effect was not observed, and charge it in the orchestrator's spend and the audit. Regression tests must fail on the old code.
